### 6.2_Re-clustering

```{r}
KC_only_obj

##> Processing after integration 
DefaultAssay(KC_only_obj) <- "integrated" 
     # no need for normalize and variable features, because here are only normalized variable features.
     # Scale the variable features. ####
     # variable features defined already in "integrated" assay
     selected_inte <- ScaleData(KC_only_obj)%>% 
                             RunPCA() %>% FindNeighbors(dims = 1:30) %>%
                             FindClusters(resolution = 0.5) %>%
                             RunUMAP(dims = 1:30) %>% 
                             RunTSNE(dims = 1:30)

##> check diff res
    # res.used <- seq(0.1,1, by=0.2)
    res.used<- c(0.7,0.9)
    # [1] 0.7 0.9. # 0.5 did before
        # Loop over and perform clustering of different resolutions
    for(i in res.used){
        selected_inte <- FindClusters(selected_inte, resolution = res.used)
    }
    
selected_inte-> KC_only_processed
save(KC_only_processed, file = "R4_6.3_KC_only_processed.Rdata")
```

### 6.4_check the marker gene expression

```{r}
DefaultAssay(selected_inte) <- "RNA" 
## define the marker genes.

## Mitotic KC: [ Proliferating KC = Mitotic cells = proliferative stem cells]
  "MKI67", "CCNB1","PCNA",
  # Basal keratinocyte (BK) = Undifferentiated keratinocytes
  "KRT14", "KRT5", "KRT15", "COL17A1",
    # Undifferentiated epidermal basal cells encompassing three quiescent (BC1–3) and proliferating (MC) subpopulations.
    # Expression of keratin 14 (K14, a marker for basal keratinocytes [Fuchs and Green, 1980]) and K15(which is enriched in stable basal cells [Porter et al., 2000]
```

## 7- Check cell type ratio change trend between studies

```{r}
library(dittoSeq)

cell_order = c(
"BAS-I",
"BAS-II",
"BAS-III",
"BAS-IV",
"BAS-V",
"SPN-I",
"SPN-II",
"SPN-III",
"SPN-IV" ,
"GRN-I",
"GRN-II",
"GRN-III")

p1<-dittoBarPlot(selected_inte, 
                 "study",  # stacks on bar
                 group.by = "cell_type_0.7", # x-axis
                 scale = "percent")+ 
                scale_x_discrete(limits = cell_order) + # Adjust the x-axis order
   scale_fill_manual(values = c("FibHSE" = "#FF0000", 
                                "FsEpi" = "#0CA14A", 
                                "PmtHEE" = "blue"))


ggsave("R4_7_split_study_cell_type_percent_ratio.pdf", plot = p1, width = 5, height =3)
```

![](images/Screenshot%202024-08-20%20at%202.02.05%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="433"}

```{r}
# Extract the data from dittoBarPlot
plot_data <- p1$data

# Recreate the bar plot using ggplot2
p2 <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = grouping, y = percent, fill = label)) + # grouping is "cell_type_0.7", 
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
      scale_x_discrete(limits = cell_order) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("FibHSE" = "#FF0000", 
                                   "FsEpi" = "#0CA14A", 
                                   "PmtHEE" = "blue")) +
      ylab("Percentage") +
      theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))+
  
# Add a fitting curve to show the trend
  geom_smooth(aes(x = factor(grouping, levels = cell_order), 
                  group = label, color = label), 
              method = "loess", 
              se = FALSE, 
              size = 1) + # label is "study" 
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))  # Ensure the y-axis range is between 0 and 1

ggsave("R4_7_study_cell_type_percent_ratio_with_curve.pdf", plot = p2, width = 5, height =3)
```

![](images/Screenshot%202024-08-20%20at%202.03.35%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="401"}

## 8- Combined DEG and marker genes

### 8.1_calculate top genes [COSG]

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
# remotes::install_github(repo = 'genecell/COSGR')
library(COSG)
library(ggpubr)

### define the deault identities.
Idents(selected_kc) <- "cell_type_0.7"

table(Idents(selected_kc))
  # BAS-I  BAS-II BAS-III  BAS-IV   BAS-V   SPN-I  SPN-II SPN-III  SPN-IV   GRN-I  GRN-II GRN-III 
  #  902     563    1652    2446    2439    3026     653    1830    2979    1168    2220    1227  

marker_cosg <- cosg(selected_kc, groups='all', 
                    assay='RNA',  ## original matrix
                    slot='data', ## use the normalized count
                    mu=1,
                    n_genes_user=50) # Number of top ranked genes returned 

# Check the marker genes and scores:
head(marker_cosg$names) # 12 columns = 12 cluster names
head(marker_cosg$scores)

## extract and combine top10 genes 
num=10 # define the top gene number
top_10_genes <- unlist(lapply(1:12, function(i) head(marker_cosg$names[,i], num))) # 120 top genes for 12 clusters

# save total top10 genes
save(top_10_genes, file="R4_8.1_kc_total_cluster_top_10.Rdata")
```

### 8.3_calculate_top_genes [Seurat]

```{r}
library(Seurat)
## marker gene calculate [only top10][method_2]
DefaultAssay(selected_kc) <- "RNA"
Idents(selected_kc)="cell_type_0.7"
markers_celltype <- FindAllMarkers(selected_kc, only.pos = TRUE, 
                                    min.pct = 0.3, 
                                    logfc.threshold = 0.3,
                                    test.use = "wilcox") 
## extract top10 genes
markers_celltype %>%group_by(cluster) %>%top_n(n = 10, wt = avg_log2FC) -> top10_marker_genes
        # [wt] :: The variable to use for ordering.


# save total top10 genes
save(top10_marker_genes, file="R4_8.3_kc_total_cluster_top_10_seurat.Rdata")
```

### 8.5\_[Seurat] Identify conserved cell type markers [Seurat]

-   To identify canonical cell type marker genes that are conserved across conditions, we provide the [`FindConservedMarkers()`](https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/findconservedmarkers) function.

-   <https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/integration_introduction>

```{r}
    # BiocManager::install('multtest')
    # install.packages('metap')
# calculate all converserved markers
cluster_name<-unique(markers_celltype$cluster)
cluster_name # 12 cluster name

# cluster_1_marker_table<- FindConservedMarkers(selected_kc, ident.1 = cluster_name[1], grouping.var = "study", verbose = TRUE) # table
# head(row.names(cluster_1_marker_table),10) # top 10 genes

# batch to combine all top10 markers
top_10_covered_markers <- unlist(lapply(1:12, function(i) head(row.names(FindConservedMarkers(selected_kc, ident.1 = cluster_name[i], grouping.var = "study", verbose = TRUE))))) # only 72 genes

# save
save(top_10_covered_markers, file= "R4_8.5_top10_coversed_markers.Rdata")
```

### 9.2-FibHSE

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
# remotes::install_github(repo = 'genecell/COSGR')
library(COSG)
library(ggpubr)

## subset for FsEpi KC
kc_id <- subset(selected_kc@meta.data, study=="FibHSE") 
FibHSE_seurat <- subset(selected_kc, cells=row.names(kc_id))

Idents(FibHSE_seurat) <- "cell_type_0.7"

DefaultAssay(FibHSE_seurat)<- 'RNA'

# When I removed the celltype that had only 1 cell, it worked! Besides, I think calculate markers for a celltype with small population (less than 10 cells or more) may be not reliable, so I filtered these celltypes before running cosg.

# filter the group, remove low cell number grouo for marker gene calculation, keep ony clusters >=10 cells
groups_selected <- names(table(FibHSE_seurat$cell_type_0.7)[table(FibHSE_seurat$cell_type_0.7) >= 10]) # only 9 groups

clusters_of_interest <- groups_selected
  # "BAS-I"   "BAS-II"  "BAS-III" "BAS-IV"  "BAS-V"   "SPN-IV"  "GRN-I"   "GRN-II"  "GRN-III"

new_filtered_seurat <- subset(FibHSE_seurat, 
                       cell_type_0.7 %in% clusters_of_interest)

modi_FibHSE<-new_filtered_seurat # filtered FibHSE

save(modi_FibHSE,file="R4_9.2_filtered_FibHSE_9_clusters.Rdata")

## COSG 
marker_cosg <- cosg(modi_FibHSE, 
                    groups='all', 
                    assay='RNA',  ## original matrix
                    slot='data', ## use the normalized count
                    mu=1,
                    n_genes_user=50) # Number of top ranked genes returned 

## extract and combine top10 genes 
num=10 # define the top gene number
top_10_genes <- unlist(lapply(1:9, function(i) head(marker_cosg$names[,i], num))) # 90 top genes for 9 clusters

# save total top10 genes
save(top_10_genes, file="R4_9.2_filtered_FibHSE_kc_total_cluster_top_10.Rdata")
```

### 9.3-PmtHEE

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
# remotes::install_github(repo = 'genecell/COSGR')
library(COSG)
library(ggpubr)

## subset for FsEpi KC
kc_id <- subset(selected_kc@meta.data, study=="PmtHEE") 
PmtHEE_seurat <- subset(selected_kc, cells=row.names(kc_id))

Idents(PmtHEE_seurat) <- "cell_type_0.7"
DefaultAssay(PmtHEE_seurat)<- 'RNA'

# When I removed the celltype that had only 1 cell, it worked! Besides, I think calculate markers for a celltype with small population (less than 10 cells or more) may be not reliable, so I filtered these celltypes before running cosg.

# filter the group, remove low cell number grouo for marker gene calculation, keep ony clusters >=10 cells
groups_selected <- names(table(PmtHEE_seurat$cell_type_0.7)[table(PmtHEE_seurat$cell_type_0.7) >= 10]) # only 10 groups

clusters_of_interest <- groups_selected
  # [1] "BAS-II"  "BAS-III" "BAS-IV"  "BAS-V"   "SPN-I"   "SPN-III" "SPN-IV"  "GRN-I"   "GRN-II" "GRN-III"

new_filtered_seurat <- subset(PmtHEE_seurat, 
                       cell_type_0.7 %in% clusters_of_interest)

modi_PmtHEE<-new_filtered_seurat # filtered FibHSE

save(modi_PmtHEE,file="R4_9.3_filtered_PmtHEE_10_clusters.Rdata")

## COSG 
marker_cosg <- cosg(modi_PmtHEE, 
                    groups='all', 
                    assay='RNA',  ## original matrix
                    slot='data', ## use the normalized count
                    mu=1,
                    n_genes_user=50) # Number of top ranked genes returned 

## extract and combine top10 genes 
num=10 # define the top gene number
top_10_genes <- unlist(lapply(1:10, function(i) head(marker_cosg$names[,i], num))) # 100 top genes for 10 clusters

# save total top10 genes
save(top_10_genes, file="R4_9.3_filtered_PmtHEE_kc_total_cluster_top_10.Rdata")
```

## 10- [ROGUE] Redo the purity analysis

```{r}
library(ROGUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)

#> seurat obj
selected_kc-> selected_inte # the seurat integrated object

#> extract count matrix
DefaultAssay(selected_inte) <- "RNA" 

expr_seurat_inte <- GetAssayData(selected_inte , slot="counts") %>% as.matrix() # rowname is gene name, col name is cell_id

#> Expression entropy model
ent.res <- SE_fun(expr_seurat_inte)  # To apply the S-E model, we calculate the expression entropy for each gene 
head(ent.res)

##> calculate rogue
rogue.value <- CalculateRogue(ent.res, platform = "UMI")
rogue.value # 0.32, thus confirming their heterogeneity... >0.9 is 

#> Calculate the ROGUE value  for each study
rogue.res <- rogue(expr_seurat_inte, 
                   labels = selected_inte$study, 
                   samples = selected_inte$cell_type_0.7, 
                   platform = "UMI", span = 0.6)

rogue.res
```

```{r}
# convert matirx count
library(reshape2)
rogue.res-> wide_data
wide_data$cell_type_0.7<-rownames(wide_data)

long_data<- melt(wide_data,
                 id.vars = c("cell_type_0.7"),
                 measure.vars = c(1:3),
                 variable.name = "study",
                 value.name = "ROGUE")
```
